An experimental dataset for indoor localization using angle of arrival and RSS measurements
abstract: Indoor positioning systems based on Bluetooth 5.1 Direction Finding technology have recently attracted significant attention due to their capability to estimate the Angle of Arrival (AoA) of radio signals using commercial off-the-shelf devices. Despite this progress, the availability of large-scale, well-annotated experimental datasets collected under realistic conditions remains limited. This paper presents a comprehensive experimental dataset for indoor localization based on BLE 5.1 devices, providing synchronized azimuth and elevation AoA measurements together with Received Signal Strength (RSS) values and precise ground-truth annotations. Data were acquired in a 110 m2 indoor environment with an adjacent corridor, deploying nine anchors in two configurations (wall-mounted and ceiling-mounted) and two wearable BLE tags. The campaign covers three scenarios: calibration (187 static reference points), static measurements with body orientation variations, and multiple mobility use-cases reproducing realistic walking patterns and posture changes. Overall, more than 4.5 million samples were collected. A preliminary analysis highlights the impact of anchor geometry, field of view, and body shadowing on angular accuracy. The dataset is publicly available and provides a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating angle-based localization, fingerprinting, filtering, and machine-learning approaches in realistic indoor environments.

title: Optimize aggregation latency of battery-free sensor network: Constructing the Battery-Free/Battery-Powered Hybrid Network
A multi-objective task offloading and resource allocation in blockchain-enabled IoT networks
abstract: The integration of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) and Blockchain has emerged as an efficient approach to support the development of secure and delay-sensitive Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Despite these advantages, blockchain-enabled IoT systems face a fundamental challenge because the security and trust benefits of blockchain are accompanied by additional computation and communication overheads that can degrade latency and energy efficiency in resource-constrained environments. This paper develops a unified multi-objective optimization framework for task offloading and resource allocation in blockchain-enabled IoT networks. The considered system architecture incorporates IoT devices, MEC servers, and a cloud data center while explicitly modeling blockchain operations as part of the offloading process. A multi-objective optimization problem is formulated to jointly minimize total system latency and energy consumption while maximizing the aggregate reputation of the selected blockchain management nodes. To solve this problem, two evolutionary solution approaches are employed. The Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is used to identify Pareto-optimal trade-off solutions, and a Genetic Algorithm (GA) is adopted to solve a weighted-sum scalarized formulation. Comprehensive simulation results indicate a demonstrable trade-off between latency and energy consumption. Specifically, the analysis reveals that prioritizing high-reputation nodes for blockchain consensus roles significantly reduces transaction verification latency, thereby enhancing the overall system performance despite the operational overheads. The framework allows stakeholders to select solutions that best meet specific IoT application requirements.

title: Delay-aware satellite networks traffic optimization using GNN-based attention and reinforcement learning
Slice-aware and cryptographically verifiable PoR for O-RAN systems
abstract: The integrity and availability of outsourced data are critical concerns in open and distributed cloud-native infrastructures such as the O-RAN architecture. Existing Proof of Retrievability (PoR) schemes, though effective in traditional settings, are insufficient to address the unique challenges of O-RAN, particularly its heterogeneous slice-specific service requirements, dynamic control loops, and auditability constraints. In this paper, we propose a novel framework that integrates PoR mechanisms into the operational fabric of O-RAN by leveraging its native control architecture. Specifically, we introduce ASAP-CD (Attested Slice-Aware PoR with Challenge Diversity), a dynamic and policy-driven auditing protocol tailored to per-slice service-level agreements, and CPT-PoR (Commitment-Packed Tags for PoR), a lightweight, commitment-based construction that supports efficient designated-verifier auditing without relying on expensive cryptographic primitives. Our design incorporates Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)-based attestation, entropy-bound challenge generation, and real-time PoR coordination via xApps and rApps. Through formal analysis and prototype implementation, we demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves strong correctness, soundness, and retrievability guarantees, while maintaining scalability and modest overhead, making it suitable for deployment in practical O-RAN environments.

title: RATIO: Redundancy-controlled stochastic routing for reliable vehicular multi-hop networking
abstract: Reliable, low-latency multi-hop data delivery in vehicular networks is increasingly demanded, yet remains challenging due to frequent route failures caused by high mobility and intermittent blockage. While redundancy-based routing enhances robustness by forwarding packets over multiple paths, over-replication intensifies contention and introduces additional delay, highlighting the need to carefully managing redundancy--reliability trade-off. However, conventional deterministic multi-path replication typically duplicates packets to an integer number of branches, making the redundancy level hard to tune and adapt to time-varying network dynamics in vehicular networks. To this end, Redundancy-Controlled Stochastic (RATIO) routing is proposed in this paper. For each active flow, RATIO constructs a weighted reduced directed acyclic graph (DAG) as the routing structure, where edge weights specify per-link forwarding probabilities. At fork nodes, the aggregate outgoing forwarding probability is allowed to exceed one and a modulo-based stochastic forwarding rule is employed to guarantee feasible forwarding, thereby enabling continuously controllable redundancy. An idealized RATIO design is formulated as a load-minimizing optimization subject to per-flow timely-reliability and link-capacity constraints, but the problem is generally intractable under time-varying wireless dynamics. Accordingly, a practical heuristic, termed H-RATIO, is developed. H-RATIO constructs a compact reduced DAG by taking the union of candidate paths and optimizes forwarding probabilities via local scoring and replication-adjustment iterations. Extensive trace-driven SUMO/ns-3 co-simulations demonstrate that RATIO/H-RATIO consistently achieves the highest timely PDR compared to baselines, while providing substantially better delivery efficiency, especially under high-load scenarios.

SPARC: Disrupting adversarial WiFi sensing with communication-safe perturbations
abstract: WiFi sensing leverages fine-grained Channel State Information (CSI) to enable applications such as occupancy detection, activity recognition, and gesture tracking. However, the same signals can be passively intercepted by nearby receivers, allowing adversaries to infer sensitive behavioral information without accessing network credentials or interacting with the system. This form of adversarial WiFi sensing is difficult to detect and cannot be mitigated through traditional security mechanisms. Defending against such inference is challenging due to the dual role of CSI: while it encodes information useful for sensing, it is also critical for communication tasks such as channel equalization and rate adaptation. Naive perturbations can degrade signal quality, while existing adversarial defenses often rely on unrealistic white-box assumptions about the attacker’s model. In this paper, we introduce SPARC, a sparse and communication-aware perturbation framework for defending against CSI-based inference. SPARC identifies a small subset of highly informative time-subcarrier elements using SSPOC and perturbs only these components under an explicit SNR constraint. This ensures that adversarial inference is disrupted while preserving communication reliability. The approach operates in a fully black-box setting and does not require access to the adversary’s model or training data. We evaluate SPARC across multiple WiFi sensing tasks, including occupancy detection, activity recognition, and gesture classification. Our results show that SPARC reduces adversarial accuracy by up to 22\% while maintaining SNR deviations within 4 dB. These results demonstrate that targeted, communication-safe perturbations provide an effective and practical mechanism for preserving privacy in WiFi sensing systems.

In-network algorithms for embedding a Multilayer Perceptron into a Wireless Sensor Network
abstract: This work presents a fully distributed framework for embedding a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) directly into the topology of a Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). Unlike existing approaches that either centralize neural computation or assign full neural models to individual nodes, the proposed architecture maps each neuron of the MLP to a physical sensor, enabling both forward inference and gradient-based training to emerge solely from local message exchanges. We provide a rigorous mathematical formulation of the distributed forward and backward recursions and derive explicit expressions for the gradients required to train the embedded model. Two explicit in-network algorithms are introduced, which allow each node to compute both activations and gradient updates using only local message exchanges. Cost analysis demonstrates that the per-node energy cost is independent of the network size and of the network topology. Furthermore, the per-node computational cost depends only on local node degree rather than the global network size, ensuring scalability to large networks. Numerical experiments on several network topologies suggest that all topologies exhibit a clear convergence trend with convergence speed depending on graph connectivity, and that the MSE of the MLP under failure conditions evolves, on average, in a similar manner to the no-failure case. Overall, this work establishes a practical foundation for deploying neural models as native, fully distributed processes within large-scale resource-constrained WSNs.

A geo-aware UAV system for detecting non-compliant parking in open parking facilities
abstract: Non-compliant parking in open parking facilities remains a persistent challenge in urban environments, reducing parking efficiency, obstructing access, and undermining the reliability of smart parking systems. Existing vision-based monitoring approaches predominantly rely on fixed camera infrastructure, which is limited in spatial coverage and often lacks location-referencing capabilities for parking violations. This paper proposes a geo-aware system based on an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) for detecting non-compliant parking using geo-tagged imagery. The proposed system integrates autonomous UAV patrol, frame-level UAV geolocation extraction, and deep learning-based object detection to identify vehicles parked outside designated spaces and associate each detection event with the corresponding UAV telemetry data. A processing pipeline synchronizes video frames with telemetry data, enabling the generation of geo-referenced outputs for enforcement and navigation purposes. The system is evaluated through real-world experiments conducted in an open parking facility, using a YOLOv8-based detection model trained on a custom annotated dataset. Experimental results show that the system achieves an accuracy of 99.56% with zero observed false positives under the tested conditions (evaluated dataset and post-processing pipelines), while providing reliable location-referencing information for detected parking violations. The proposed approach enables mobile, geo-aware sensing of parking facilities, addresses key limitations of static monitoring systems, and provides a practical solution for improving parking compliance, reducing operational inefficiencies, and supporting sustainable urban mobility management.

MF-EFLJD: Multi-faceted ensemble federated learning for jamming detection in private 5G-enabled IIoT networks
abstract: Wireless network security is a growing concern in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) as jamming attacks disrupt communication of IIoT entities in Private 5G networks. While machine learning (ML) algorithms detect jamming attacks effectively, centralized data collection from entities compromises sensitive information and privacy in distributed IIoT environment. This article presents a multi-faceted ensemble federated learning-based jamming detection framework, MF-EFLJD, to detect and further improve detection performance. To address the issue of non-independent and identical distribution (non-IID) and high-dimensional wireless channel data persisting across femtocells, this framework proposes sequential integration of Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) values to obtain optimized and structured data. Moreover, the framework trains 1D-CNN-based Federated Learning (FL) component on optimized data of entities to detect jamming attacks under non-IID conditions at each femtocell. Furthermore, to boost the performance detection of FL under non-IID, we propose Random Forest (RF)-based stacking ensemble component with an unweighted majority soft voting approach. Under non-IID setting α = 0.7 , the proposed system demonstrates that FL achieves accuracies of 0.9376 ( ± 0.0134 ) , 0.8806 ( ± 0.0178 ) , and 0.9576 ( ± 0.0169 ) for femtocells F 1 , F 2 , and F 3 , respectively, in detecting jammed and non-jammed signals. Additionally, the ensemble component achieves 0.9963 ( ± 0.0031 ) accuracy, depicting improvement in performance across femtocells.
